<!-- pr-reviewer: 7bc45283c08b314daaabfa44536c65cdf2e3037f -->
**Not built - needs a maintainer look.** No code defects found. The PR changes where a dependency comes from (`ruststep` and the proc-macro `ruststep-derive` now come from a git rev instead of crates.io, via `[patch.crates-io]` in `Cargo.toml`). Under the review rules, a change to dependencies is read but not compiled until the maintainer decides on it. That decision is the one you asked to have flagged: this would be the workspace's first git dependency.

Thank you for the thorough write-up and the bisection. The root-cause analysis checks out against upstream.

### What looks good
- The fix is the upstream one, not a local text hack. ricosjp/ruststep@90fdc935 wraps the list body in `opt_(...)` and maps `None` to `Parameter::List(vec![])`.
- `Cargo.lock` changes only the two `source` lines (and drops their checksums). No version or transitive dependency drift, and truck-stepio's `ruststep = "0.4"` resolves to the same patched crate.
- The pin is to an exact `rev`, so builds are reproducible. The `Cargo.toml` comment says why the pin exists and when to drop it.
- Fixture `testdata/models/empty_list.step` is the repo's own `box.step` plus one line (`#166 = DRAUGHTING_MODEL('', (), #2);`, checked with `diff`). It is self-made, small and clean-room safe. The pinning test asserts the same 12-facet box.
- Body is complete: what changed, red proof, `Changelog:` line, `Fixes #887`, conventional subject. No process files are touched (no `PROCESS_VERSION` bump needed). No production code changed, so there are no new `unwrap`/`expect` and no file-length or provenance issues.

### What the pinned rev changes vs the released 0.4.0 (read via the GitHub compare API, `ruststep-v0.4.0...90fdc935`)
The rev is 3 commits past the tag but changes only 2 files, both in the parser. There are no `build.rs` changes and no changes to `ruststep-derive` source.
1. `ruststep/src/parser/exchange/parameter.rs`: the empty-list fix (this PR's point).
2. `ruststep/src/parser/token.rs` (4197eee8, "handle escape string sequence"): a string now reads `''` inside quotes as one `'`, as ISO 10303-21 specifies. **The PR body does not mention this second change**, but the pin brings it in.

### Parser-safety check (what I judged without building)
- **Files that parsed before parse the same.** Before the pin, `()` as a value was always a parse failure, and so was a `''` inside a string (the string closed early and the next token was garbage). Neither construct can appear in a file that imported before, so the parse result of every previously-importing file is unchanged. Entity-level empty lists such as `LENGTH_UNIT()` use a different path and are untouched, as you noted. `$`, `*` and nested lists (`((1,2),())`) go through the same `parameter` alternatives as before. Only the outer list is now optional.
- **Degenerate input stays clean, with no hang or unbounded loop.** `opt_(comma_separated(parameter))` either consumes at least one parameter or returns `None` without consuming anything, so the enclosing combinators cannot loop on zero-length matches. In the string parser, both branches of `many0` consume input (`''` = 2 chars, any other char = 1). Neither change adds recursion, index math or allocation. Recursion depth on nested lists is the same as on 0.4.0. Empty string `''` followed by `,` or `)` still parses as an empty string, because `tag("''")` needs two quotes right after the opening one.
- The existing `step_garbage_is_clean_error_never_panic` test still covers garbage input. It was not run here (see below).

### Local results
| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| Fetch + head check | `7bc45283` confirmed |
| Trial merge with `origin/main` | clean, no conflicts |
| `cargo build` / `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test import` / clippy | **not run**: dependency source change, held for the maintainer |

### Requested before merge
None. No code defects found.

### For the maintainer (the decision this PR asks for)
- **Accept a git dependency?** Options: (a) take this pin as is (exact rev, small audited delta, a comment that says to drop it at the next ruststep release); (b) ask for the contributor's patch-fork route (same shape, different host); (c) wait for an upstream release (ricosjp/ruststep#256, no date). If you accept it, a builder run of `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test import` (expect 23 passed) and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` closes the gap left here.
- Practical effects of a git source: `Cargo.lock` has no checksum for the two crates, and a cold build (CI `release.yml`, a fresh clone, any fork) fetches from github.com/ricosjp/ruststep instead of crates.io. If that repository is rewritten or deleted, the build breaks, but the code cannot change silently, because the rev is pinned.

### Notes (non-blocking)
- Consider mentioning the escape-string change (4197eee8) in the PR body and the `Cargo.toml` comment, so whoever later drops the pin knows two behaviours ride on it. A one-line test, for example a fixture name `'O''Brien'` that imports, would pin it too.
- The error-message half of #887 (pointing at `DATA;` instead of the failing entity) stays open as you note. A follow-up issue for it would keep it tracked.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

**Ready for the maintainer to merge.** This is the built follow-up to my earlier review. The maintainer has accepted the pinned ruststep git dependency, so this time I built and tested the same head, `7bc45283`, merged with current `origin/main`.

### Local results (trial merge with `origin/main`: clean)
| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| Build: `ruststep` / `ruststep-derive` from git rev `90fdc935` | compiled cleanly |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test import` (includes the new `step_file_with_empty_parameter_list_imports` and `step_garbage_is_clean_error_never_panic`) | 23 passed, 0 failed |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test solid_law` (STEP-backed solids) | 4 passed, 0 failed |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test commands_undo` (STEP import via commands) | 32 passed, 0 failed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

Not run: the UI suites (unaffected by this PR; main's `camcraft-ui` lib test is red for an unrelated reason, #907 / PR #908) and the release-tier heavy lanes.

### Requested before merge
None.

### Notes (non-blocking)
The notes from my earlier review still apply. Consider mentioning the escape-string fix (4197eee8) that the pinned rev also brings in, and filing a follow-up for the error-location half of #887.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
